report:
### Conclusion
**Yes**, clinical evidence supports using honey to relieve acute cough in children **aged 1 year and older**.

### Scientific Evidence & Mechanism
Systematic reviews, including Cochrane evaluations, demonstrate that honey reduces cough frequency and severity compared to no treatment, placebos, or antihistamines like diphenhydramine, while improving sleep quality for both children and parents (https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD007094_honey-acute-cough-children, https://publications.aap.org/aapnews/article/29/2/2/22340/Honey-helps-quiet-cough).

Mechanistically, honey functions primarily as a demulcent. Its high viscosity and sweetness trigger reflex salivation and airway mucus secretion, creating a soothing barrier over the pharyngeal mucosa that calms the cough reflex (https://www.mayoclinic.org/symptoms/cough/expert-answers/honey/faq-20058031). Darker honey varieties also offer antioxidant and mild antibacterial properties that may further soothe respiratory tract inflammation.

### Critical Safety Warning
Honey **must never** be given to infants under 12 months of age. An infant's immature digestive tract cannot inhibit *Clostridium botulinum* endospores, which can germinate and cause life-threatening infant botulism (https://publications.aap.org/aapnews/news/13225/Remind-families-honey-can-cause-infant-botulism). For children over age 1, medical organizations recommend honey as a safe, effective alternative to over-the-counter cough medications.
